title: JSX Code Practice
summary: Practice challenge: build a React app from scratch that renders a heading and an unordered list of three items, then a walkthrough of the solution including the single-parent rule and how the editor's auto-format handles empty elements.

concepts.heading: Setup of the challenge
points: Fork the provided CodeSandbox so changes are saved to your account. index.html already contains the div#root; index.js has been emptied so the whole React app is written from scratch.
The code comments in the sandbox list the steps to complete one by one.

concepts.heading: Solution walkthrough
points: Import React from 'react' and ReactDOM from 'react-dom' (both packages are already installed in the sandbox, but must be imported before use).
Call ReactDOM.render with two minimum arguments: what to show and where to show it. Start with an h1 heading, with document.getElementById('root') as the target.
To add a ul next to the h1, wrap both in a div, because render takes one element only; the div can have any number of children.
Add three li elements inside the ul with content (bacon, noodles, a third food).
Saving (Cmd/Ctrl+S) runs the formatter (prettifier). An li with nothing inside gets rewritten as a self-closing tag (<li />), like img or link; adding text content avoids that rewrite.

concepts.heading: Learning approach
points: Repeating the from-scratch render steps builds muscle memory. A completed sandbox is linked in the resources for comparison.

task.name: JSX code practice: favourite foods list
task.starting_point: Forked CodeSandbox with empty index.js and a div#root in index.html
task.goal: Create a React app from scratch showing an h1 and an unordered list with three list items
steps: Call ReactDOM.render with a wrapper div as the first argument, containing an h1 heading and a ul.
Add three li elements with text to the ul.
Pass document.getElementById('root') as the second argument.
task.expected_result: Page with a heading and a bulleted list of three favourite foods.

pitfalls: Rendering a heading and a list as siblings without a wrapper throws a syntax error.
Empty elements are rewritten as self-closing tags by the formatter; give list items text.
The reference repo's App.jsx goes beyond the task (variables, extra ol, notes text); the core requirement (h1, ul, 3 li) is satisfied.
